answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to maintain a unique, non-transferable meadow of attested work history that grows slowly like a field of violet flowers after rain. An attacker creating many identities would face the cost of waiting for each to accumulate genuine peer attestations, similar to how an ocean of fakes cannot instantly flood a reputation system without real signals. This delays and raises the expense of mass spoofing.
